link_power_management_states.name: Active
link_power_management_states.description: Full operation at the trained NVHS rate; flits flow in both directions; CRC + replay active. Lane width = full brick (8 pairs/direction) or reduced after lane deconfigure.

link_power_management_states.name: Low-power link standby
link_power_management_states.description: Idle link enters a low-power state; sub-link in electrical idle. Exit re-trains/realigns the NVHS lanes.
link_power_management_states.exit_latency_estimate: training/alignment time (PAM4 eye adaptation at Gen4 adds latency)

link_power_management_states.name: Link off
link_power_management_states.description: Link not trained / powered down; full training required to bring it up.

low_power_modes_summary.Active: Full operational power at the trained NVHS rate (NRZ Gen1-3 / PAM4 Gen4).
low_power_modes_summary.Sleep: Sub-link electrical idle; re-train/realign on exit.
low_power_modes_summary.Down: Link powered down; full bring-up required.

fields.gen4_power_considerations: At Gen4 the PAM4 NVHS SerDes (four-level slicer, stronger CTLE/DFE, TX equalizer) and the larger link count (18 links on H100) dominate active interconnect power, raising the value of disciplined link Sleep states. Re-entry from Sleep must re-train/realign the NVHS lanes (PAM4 eye adaptation), increasing exit latency versus NRZ generations.
fields.notes: NVLink power management is coordinated with the GPU's overall power state. Idle links can drop to a low-power Sleep state and re-train on demand; unused NVLinks stay Down. The NVHS PHY (especially PAM4 at Gen4) is the dominant interconnect power consumer, so link-state discipline directly affects platform power.

extraction_hints: Look for power-domain partitioning, supply nets.
